tasks.title: Choose a Robust Typical Order Value
tasks.context: Most orders are between 500 and 2500, but one corporate order is 250000.
tasks.goal: Choose a summary that represents a typical order without being dominated by the extreme value.
tasks.prompt: Which should you report as the typical order value?
hints: The data contains an extreme high value.
The mean is sensitive to outliers.
The median is robust to extreme observations.
tasks.explanation: The median depends on rank rather than the magnitude of the extreme value, so it is usually a better description of a skewed typical order.

tasks.title: Recognize the Pandas GroupBy Pattern
tasks.context: You need one revenue total per region from a dataframe named df.
tasks.goal: Recognize the standard Pandas grouping pattern.
tasks.prompt: Which expression groups by region and sums revenue?
hints: Aggregate the revenue Series with sum().
tasks.explanation: groupby defines the groups and sum reduces the revenue values within each group.

tasks.title: Fix a Conversion Rate Denominator
tasks.context: A marketer reports conversions divided by all site visits, but the campaign only reached a subset of visitors.
tasks.goal: Use a denominator aligned with the population exposed to the campaign.
tasks.prompt: Which conversion rate is most diagnostic for campaign performance?
tasks.expectedAnswer: Campaign conversions divided by eligible campaign-exposed visitors
hints: A rate needs a denominator from the relevant population.
Unexposed traffic dilutes the campaign measure.
Use people eligible and exposed to the campaign.
tasks.explanation: A numerator and denominator must describe the same population. Otherwise the rate mixes campaign performance with unrelated traffic.
options: Campaign conversions divided by eligible campaign-exposed visitors
Campaign conversions divided by employee count
All purchases divided by all historical visits
Campaign spend divided by page views

tasks.title: Handle a Suspicious Outlier
tasks.context: One order amount is 100 times larger than normal. It may be a valid enterprise order or a decimal-entry error.
tasks.expectedAnswer: Investigate against source records and business rules before deciding whether to keep, correct, cap, or exclude it
hints: Outlier does not automatically mean error.
Validate against source evidence and a documented rule.
tasks.explanation: Professional cleaning distinguishes unusual-but-valid values from errors. The treatment should be documented and reproducible.
options: Investigate against source records and business rules before deciding whether to keep, correct, cap, or exclude it
Replace it with zero without checking
Duplicate it to balance the data

tasks.title: Interpret an Inconclusive A/B Test
tasks.context: An A/B test shows a promising 4% lift but has a very wide confidence interval that includes meaningful harm and meaningful gain.
tasks.goal: Avoid treating uncertainty as proof of no effect.
tasks.expectedAnswer: The test is inconclusive; report the interval and effect estimate, check power/sample size, and gather more evidence if the decision value justifies it
hints: A non-significant result is not proof of zero effect.
The interval contains a wide range of plausible effects.
Discuss effect size, uncertainty and power.
tasks.explanation: Decision-quality experiment reporting includes the estimated effect and uncertainty, not only a binary significance label.
options: The test is inconclusive; report the interval and effect estimate, check power/sample size, and gather more evidence if the decision value justifies it
The treatment definitely has zero effect

tasks.title: Build a Revenue Metric Tree
tasks.context: Revenue fell 12%. Leadership wants a framework that separates traffic, conversion and order-value drivers.
tasks.goal: Decompose the top-line outcome into actionable components.
tasks.expectedAnswer: Revenue = traffic × conversion rate × average order value, then drill into the drivers of each component
hints: Start with an identity that reconstructs revenue.
Then drill into drivers below each branch.
tasks.explanation: A metric tree connects the executive outcome to operational drivers and makes diagnostic analysis more systematic.
options: Revenue = traffic × conversion rate × average order value, then drill into the drivers of each component
